acceptance: tests/test_index_release.py: with a fake index that lists the version after N polls, the install runs exactly once, after it appears; with a fake index that never lists it, the script fails after the bounded wait with a message naming the version and the wait; the poll request carries Cache-Control: no-cache.
A test shows that an install failure after the version is listed fails immediately, with no retry.
publish.yml distribution-verify has timeout-minutes: 20, above the 8-minute poll bound plus install time; all existing tests in tests/test_index_release.py still pass.
docs/operations/release-gates.md, section After the tag, says the verify step waits up to 8 minutes for the index to list the version.
context: 2026-11-14 done in https://github.com/joeharris76/tractable/pull/75 (merge 2ef7b7c, head 6ff3751; CI test (3.10), test (3.13), release-gate1 green). scripts/verify_index_release.py polls https://pypi.org/simple/tractable/ with Accept: application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+json and Cache-Control: no-cache for up to 480 s, polling again only on 5xx and failing at once on any other HTTP error or malformed listing, then installs once; interval, deadline, clock, sleep and fetch are injectable. New tests in tests/test_index_release.py: install runs exactly once after the listing appears; a never-listed version fails naming the version and 480s; the poll carries Cache-Control: no-cache (fake and default fetch); an install failure after listing is not retried and stops polling. publish.yml distribution-verify timeout-minutes: 20. release-gates.md After the tag states the 8-minute wait. Full suite 505 passed; ruff clean. Takes effect for tags created after 2ef7b7c.
description:
Defect. `distribution-verify` (publish.yml, the opt-in PyPI run) installs `tractable[mcp]==$VERSION` from https://pypi.org/simple seconds after `pypi-publish` finishes. PyPI's simple index can lag an upload by a minute or more, so the install fails with "there is no version of tractable[mcp]==X" even though the upload succeeded and the same job already verified both files' hashes from PyPI's JSON API. Observed on the 1.1.1 run (links): attempts 1 and 2 failed this way at 12:53 and 12:54 UTC; the same uv command failed locally at 12:54 and succeeded about two minutes later; attempt 3 passed unchanged. Effect: the run is marked failed, needs a manual job rerun, and looks like a broken release.

Decision (owner, 2026-11-14): poll, then install once. In scripts/verify_index_release.py, before the fresh install, request https://pypi.org/simple/tractable/ (PEP 691 JSON, with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, because PyPI serves that page with max-age=600) until it lists the version, for at most 8 minutes; then run the existing install once. Raise distribution-verify's `timeout-minutes` from 10 to 20 so the job timeout cannot cut the wait short.

Guardrails:
- Never upload again, start another publish run, or retry the install itself.
- Keep `uv --no-config --no-cache` and the isolated environment unchanged.
- Do not change which bytes are checked, the version checks, or the MCP initialize/tools-list check.
- The wait polls one condition (version listed). A transient 5xx is polled again; any other HTTP error or malformed response fails at once.
- Effective only for tags created after it lands: a dispatch runs the workflow stored at its tag.
